title: paged KV cache: block allocator refactor, reuse and locality-aware pinning
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: The paged KV cache block manager has accumulated incremental fixes for allocator reuse and pinning, but the allocator code is fragmented and causes alloc/free churn under high-concurrency workloads (continuous batching + long-context models). This PR refactors the block allocator, introduces reuse-friendly APIs, and adds locality-aware pinning heuristics to reduce remote page thrash. Goals: 1) Reduce allocation churn and GC pressure during high QPS streaming workloads. 2) Improve tail latency by keeping hot KV pages pinned near serving threads. 3) Preserve backwards compatibility and enable gradual rollout.

Summary of changes: - Introduced BlockPool abstraction that centralizes block allocation/free and keeps per-gpu free-lists to avoid cross-device contention. - Implemented fast-path reuse: allocate_reuse() which prefers recently-freed blocks with matching size and alignment to avoid zeroing and remap costs. - Locality-aware pinning: pin hints propagate with request affinity so long-lived contexts keep their pages pinned on the same device/NUMA domain. - Pin TTL & eviction policies: configurable TTLs per-model and per-workload; added decay-based eviction to allow bursty reuse. - Reduced atomic contention via sharded freelists and optimistic try-claim logic. - Added metrics: block_pool_hits, block_pool_misses, pin_locality_ratio, pin_evictions, reuse_success_rate. - Unit + integration tests for allocator reuse and pinning invariants. - Perf microbench harness and a scaled canary across dedicated pool.

Checklist: - [x] Core allocator refactor + unit tests - [x] Integration tests for continuous batching workload - [x] Benchmarks: latency and throughput - [x] Add metrics & dashboards - [x] Backwards compatibility and feature-flag rollout - [x] Docs and config knobs in runtime config

Performance: On a 32-GPU dedicated canary running the long-context chat workload (avg seq 2048, concurrency 512), observed: - 12% median token latency reduction - 18% 95p token latency reduction - 20% throughput improvement (tokens/sec) - 28% reduction in peak device memory fragmentation (measured via page reuse counters)

Compatibility & rollout: Changes guarded behind feature-flag runtime.paged_kv.new_allocator (default=false). Gradual rollout plan: canary on dedicated -> beta in hosted region with low-traffic tenants -> global rollout after 2 weeks of stability. No client-visible API changes.
commits_summary: 5 commits: 1) introduce BlockPool + freelist sharding (core refactor) 2) add allocate_reuse fast-path and reuse heuristics 3) implement locality-aware pinning + TTL eviction 4) metrics, dashboards and tests 5) canary config + rollout script
review_conversation: Reviewer Evan: 'Can you justify the additional mutexes in BlockPool? Concerned about contention spikes.' Author: 'We shard freelists by device and size class; the scoped locks are narrow and we benchmarked under 512 concurrency - see perf section. Added optimistic try-claim to avoid lock path for common-case reuse.' Reviewer Sara: 'Pin TTL default feels high for bursty workloads.' Author: 'Added per-model TTL and decay-based eviction; default tuned conservatively. We exposed the knob in runtime config and plan to adjust after canary metrics.' Reviewer Noah: 'Where are the regressions for older small-context workloads?' Author: 'We added a fallback that keeps previous allocator behavior under feature-flag off; unit tests show parity. Benchmarks show no regression for avg seq < 256.' Approvals: Evan + Sara approved after 2 iterations. Noah left an approval comment after canary numbers were posted.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (two flaky DB tests retried)
release_notes: Refactor paged KV block allocator to improve reuse and add locality-aware pinning. Expect reduced latency and better throughput for long-context, high-concurrency workloads. Feature is behind runtime.paged_kv.new_allocator and requires canary rollout.
notes: Follow-up PR planned to add model-aware size classes and finer-grained NUMA placement. Also tracking ENG-1502 for dashboard alert rules based on pin_evictions metric.
